LEARNING RARE LIFETIMES FROM LOCAL CLOCKS
Finite-error computation for driven Markov systems
Research developed 1 November 2026 (Australia/Brisbane)

Scope and status
===============
This is a self-contained mathematical construction and reproducible synthetic
calculation. It is not an experimentally validated device, an algorithm for
arbitrary unknown dynamics, or an established historical-priority claim.
Independent mathematical reconstructions and exact finite checks are included.
The positive result uses established Markov potential theory, sector estimates,
Poisson clocks and Monte Carlo. The proposed addition is the complete chain from
acquired local rate uncertainty, through uniform rare-target stability, to a
finite-error short-excursion receiver and later decisions.

Prior Astra research is bound to repository harjassand/astra-research-knowledge,
revision 51ce47ce39f976517d60e2f87bbe280b651f6056. Its 00_START_HERE.txt was the
first corpus file read. The decisive inherited obstruction is N1213's failure
of replacing a singleton return identity by a coarse-target indicator. The new
proof below is independent of any unavailable attachment from that record.
Source paths, conditions, comparisons and useful alternative failures are in
SOURCES_AND_COMPARISONS.txt and the independent notes in this package.

1. Intended consequence and exact contract
=========================================
Question: Can finite, ordinary-state calibration support reliable later
prediction of rare first-passage times in a driven stochastic system, without
waiting for those passages, preserving its entire long trajectory, or assuming
a precomputed committor? We construct such a service for the following class.

The source has a finite state space Omega and known executable maps P_a. Each
P_a is a permutation preserving the same known probability pi; uniform pi is
the principal explicit implementation. Every cycle of every P_a has length at
most ell >= 2. Independent Poisson clocks of unknown positive rates lambda_a
apply these maps. A clock mark remains observable even if its map fixes the
current state. This last requirement is an observation resource, not a
consequence of observing state changes.

INDEPENDENT AUDIT: NONREVERSIBLE SCREENED HITTING AND SHORT-CYCLE RATE STABILITY
1 November 2026

VERDICT

The two stated mathematical inequalities are correct under the finite-state
contracts below. I independently derived them and checked 240 screened-hitting
instances and 120 rate-perturbation instances in exact Fraction arithmetic.
The audit identified an algorithmic precision caveat: relative accuracy of the
screened exit rate does not always give relative accuracy of R_s because its
definition subtracts 1/s. A sufficient rare-target condition or an alternate
estimator is needed. Several interface qualifications remain essential.

FILES

exact_audit.py: independent rational generator construction, stationary-law
checks, linear solves and inequalities; no dependency on root implementation.
exact_audit_results.json: actual output from running that script.

1. CONVENTIONS AND REQUIRED INPUTS

Q is a finite irreducible continuous-time generator acting on column functions
by (Qf)(x)=sum_y q_xy f(y); its rows sum to zero. pi is its unique positive
stationary law. L=-Q. Inner products are weighted by pi. Adjoints always mean
the pi-weighted adjoint. Let H=(L+L*)/2 and assume a supplied/earned g>0 with

   <f,Hf> >= g ||f||_pi^2 whenever E_pi f=0.

This is the gap of the additive symmetric part, not merely a real-part bound on
eigenvalues of a nonnormal generator. A target A is nonempty and proper; write
p=pi(A), b=1-p, B=A^c. The promised output is

   M=E_(pi conditioned on B) tau_A.

The formula concerns this mean. It does not by itself identify a full lifetime
distribution, a worst-start mean, or a rare-event probability over a deadline.

2. FORWARD-EXIT FLUX IS CORRECT EVEN WITHOUT REVERSIBILITY

For s>0 let u=E_x exp(-s tau_A), so u=1 on A and

   (sI-Q_B)u_B=q_BA 1.

Equivalently, (L+s)u=0 on B. On A,

   (Lu)(x)=sum_(y in B) q_xy [1-u(y)].

Stationarity gives <1,Lu>=0, hence

   sum_A pi(x)(Lu)(x)=s sum_B pi(y)u(y).

Therefore the stated FORWARD exit quantity

   r_s=s+E_(pi|A) sum_(y in B) q_xy[1-u(y)]

satisfies

   p r_s=s C,   C=E_pi u.

No time-reversal, detailed balance or backward exit rates are required. Since
p<C<1 for a nontrivial finite irreducible chain and finite s>0,

   R_s=1/(p r_s)-1/s=(1-C)/(s C)>0.

The companion identity useful for an alternate estimator is

   M_s=E_(pi|B) min(tau_A,E_s),  E_s~Exp(s) independent,
